at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.10.2026) The ‘Sharaka’ project is implemented by the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) and the Italian Ministry of Interior, fully financed under the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument – Global Europe (NDICI-GE)1. IOM provides technical and operational expertise, including humanitarian border management. Italy provides expertise in maritime search and rescue (SAR), fleet maintenance, and transnational investigations. The action covers Libya’s maritime border and its southern borders with Algeria, Niger, Chad, Sudan and Egypt, including main smuggling routes. It supports Libya's Ministries of Interior, Defence, Health, Local Governance and Labour, the National Safety Authority, and other relevant SAR actors. It comprises three components: SAR at sea, SAR in the desert, and community stabilisation. The maritime component includes maintenance and equipment, coordination support via the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre and training. The desert component includes border surveillance capacity, multi-sectoral SAR, action against smuggling and trafficking networks, prosecutorial support, a biometric registration feasibility study meeting human rights standards. The community stabilisation activities aim at strengthened local governance and service delivery mechanisms and include enhancing access to essential services such as health, education or water in underserved and mobility-affected areas. Support is channelled exclusively through recognised institutions under the Government of National Unity, in line with the UN-led political process, and is subject to human rights safeguards and monitoring.
1 Regulation (EU) 2021/947 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 June 2021 establishing the
Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument – Global Europe (OJ L 209, 14.6.2021, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/947/oj).
